subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit binding tiers miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level behavior is high-confidence, but changing fallback routing can affect session state, provider/model choice, and permission boundaries for existing Discord setups.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route only non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent after explicit bindings miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor checks, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair The Fork PR First
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after conflicts, phantom-agent guards, diagnostics, and real Discord proof are addressed.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route only non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent after explicit bindings miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across the shared resolver and multi-agent/multi-account routing contract.
